_note: Spot the scam — one puzzle a day, picked by AEST day number. Hand-written and reviewed, not generated. Links use the reserved .example domain so nothing here is clickable or real. In each body, a segment with "g" is highlighted when the answer is revealed, and points at the giveaway with the same index.

body.t: Your account has an unpaid toll of $2.80.
Pay within 24 hours to avoid a $135 penalty:

giveaways: It comes from an ordinary mobile number, not from Linkt.
A tiny amount with a big penalty and a short deadline is designed to rush you.
The link isn't linkt.com.au. If you're unsure, log in to your toll account by typing the address yourself.

body.t: Update your details and pay the $1.99 redelivery fee:

giveaways: It doesn't name you, the sender or the parcel. Scams are sent to thousands of numbers at once.
Australia Post doesn't text you asking for payment or personal details.
The link isn't auspost.com.au. Sender names like "AusPost" can be faked, so the name alone proves nothing.

items.subject: Your tax refund is ready

body.t: You are eligible for a tax refund of

giveaways: Real refunds are paid into the bank account you already gave the ATO. You don't have to claim them from an email.
A 48-hour deadline is there to stop you checking first.
myGov says it never sends links to sign in. The sender address isn't my.gov.au either.

body.t: Hi Mum, I dropped my phone in the toilet.
Can you message me on WhatsApp?

giveaways: An unknown number saying it's a family member, without using their name.
Moving the chat to another app makes it harder for your phone company to flag it.
The "favour" is usually an urgent payment. Call your child on the number you already have before doing anything.

items.context: You've just tried to sign in to your email on a new laptop.

body.t: Don't share this code with anyone.

giveaways: You asked for it: it arrived right after you tried to sign in.
There's no link and nothing to reply to. It only tells you not to share the code.
If a code like this arrives when you didn't ask for one, someone may have your password. Change it.

items.subject: Your membership is on hold

body.t:
.

We couldn't process your latest payment, so your membership has been paused.
Update your card details now to keep watching.

giveaways: "Dear Customer" instead of your name. Services you pay for know your name.
It asks for card details by email. Check by opening the app or typing the website address yourself.
The sender address isn't netflix.com, even though the name says Netflix.

items.subject: You have a new message in your myGov Inbox

body.t: You have a new message from
Sign in to myGov to read it.
this email doesn't contain a link.

giveaways: It doesn't ask for anything or mention money.
It tells you to sign in yourself, instead of giving you a place to type your password.
There's no link at all, which matches how myGov says it contacts people. To be safe, still type my.gov.au yourself.

body.t: A new device was added to your account
call our fraud team now on 02 XXXX XXXX.
Do not log in until we have secured your account.

giveaways: A precise time makes it feel real. That detail is easy to make up.
The number to call is in the message itself. Call the number on the back of your card instead.
Telling you not to log in stops you seeing that nothing is wrong. Banks want you to check your account.

body.t: Your tax return has been flagged for review.
Log in within 48 hours to avoid a penalty:

giveaways: A vague problem with your tax is meant to worry you before you think it through.
A deadline and a penalty push you to act now instead of checking.
The ATO says it won't text you a link to log in to its online services. Go to my.gov.au yourself.

items.context: You booked a check-up at your local dentist last month.

body.t: Hi Sam, a reminder of your appointment with
Dr Patel on Thu 28 Nov at 10:30am.
Reply Y to confirm or call the clinic to change it.

giveaways: It matches something you booked, with the right name, day and dentist.
It only asks for a Y. No link, no payment and no personal details.

items.subject: Action required: your mailbox is 98% full

body.t: Your mailbox has almost reached its limit.
New emails will be rejected from today.
Sign in with your work password to keep receiving mail.

giveaways: A threat that mail will stop today is there to rush you.
The button goes to a site that isn't Microsoft's. Check storage in Outlook itself.
Asking you to type your password after clicking a link is how passwords get stolen.

body.t: Hi, I'm Jenny from a recruitment agency.
Your CV was recommended to us.
Part-time online work, $300 to $800 a day, no experience needed.
Add me on WhatsApp to start.

giveaways: You never sent them your CV. A vague compliment is the hook.
Big pay for easy work is the bait in task scams. You'll be asked to pay in to 'unlock' earnings.
Moving you to WhatsApp takes you away from anyone who could warn you.

items.subject: Updated bank details for invoice 4471

body.t: Please pay this month's invoice to the new account below

and update your records.

BSB 000-000  Account 0000 0000
We're in an audit, so please don't call the office this week.

giveaways: Changed bank details by email is the most common trick in business email scams. Look closely at the address too: it's "coastIine" with a capital I, not an L.
One email is not enough to send money to a new account. That's how the payment goes to the scammer.
Asking you not to call stops the one check that would catch it. Call the supplier on a number you already have.

body.t: Verify now to keep your benefits:

giveaways: A suspended card is a made-up emergency.
"Verify" means "type your details into our page".
Medicare is run by Services Australia, which says its texts won't include a link to sign in. Use the Express Plus Medicare app or my.gov.au yourself.

body.t: If you didn't place this order, call our refund team on 1800 XXX XXX.

giveaways: An expensive order you didn't make is meant to scare you into acting.
The 'refund team' will ask to install an app on your computer or for your bank details. Check your orders in the Amazon app instead.

items.context: You changed your Streamly password two minutes ago.
items.subject: Your password was changed

body.t: The password for your Streamly account
If this was you, there's nothing to do.
If it wasn't, open the Streamly app and go to Account to secure it.

giveaways: It matches what you just did.
It doesn't ask you to do anything if it was you.
It sends you to the app you already have, not to a link in the email.

body.t: Hi Karen, is this still your number?
It's Lily from the Saturday yoga class.
I've been doing really well with crypto lately, happy to show you how.

giveaways: A 'wrong number' message from a stranger opens a friendly chat. It's how many investment scams start.
After weeks of chatting, they bring up crypto and show fake profits so you'll pay in.

items.context: You ordered a pizza on Tony's website 25 minutes ago.

body.t: and should arrive in about 15 minutes.

giveaways: You placed the order, and the timing fits.
It doesn't ask for anything: no link, no payment, no reply.

items.context: You booked flights to Hobart on the Jetline website last night.
items.subject: Booking confirmed: Sydney to Hobart, 14 Dec

body.t: Thanks for booking. Your reference is
You can manage your booking in the Jetline app.

giveaways: It arrived right after you booked, with a reference you can check.
The flight details match what you chose.
It points you to the app, and asks for no payment or password. If in doubt, look the booking up yourself.

items.subject: Your page will be removed in 24 hours

body.t: We received a copyright report about your page.
If you don't appeal within 24 hours, your page will be permanently deleted.
You'll need to confirm your password and login code.

giveaways: A 24-hour threat to delete your page is there to rush you.
The link isn't facebook.com. Check alerts in the app's own notifications.
No real appeal asks for your login code. Anyone with it can take over your account.
